DIS.thesis_one_line: Best-in-class content and theme-park owner where streaming is finally turning profitable, but companywide cash generation actually fell this year.
kill_criteria: TTM free cash flow does not recover to at least $10bn by FY26 year-end (vs FY25's $10.1bn) — signals the FCF decline is structural, not timing.
ESPN/Sports segment operating income declines YoY for two consecutive quarters excluding sports-calendar effects (playoff timing).
Disney+/Hulu/Hotstar combined SVOD operating margin fails to reach double digits for full FY26 (vs the guided target).
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.5x (vs ≈1.7x now), signalling buybacks are outrunning cash generation.
FY27 guidance (to be given with FY26 Q4 results, Nov 2026) is cut from the currently-reiterated "double-digit adjusted EPS growth."
key_adverse_facts: 9-month FY26 free cash flow $5.74bn vs $7.52bn prior year (-24%); 6-month FY26 FCF down 53% YoY before partial recovery in Q3.

Q3 FY26 $812m impairment on the A+E Networks equity-method investment (Hearst JV); 1H FY26 also carried $147m equity-investment impairment, $92m severance and $422m non-cash tax charges tied to the Fubo/NFL transactions.
Sports (ESPN) segment operating income fell 17% YoY in Q3 FY26 on playoff-schedule effects and a network-carriage dispute.
International park attendance (Shanghai, Hong Kong) stayed soft through Q3 FY26 and management expects continued softness in Q4.
$50m antitrust settlement (in principle, not yet fully closed) over YouTube TV/DirecTV Stream bundling pricing; a related FuboTV antitrust suit is unresolved.
GAAP diluted EPS ($1.27-$1.51 the last two quarters) is far below and far more volatile than adjusted EPS ($2.06 in Q3) due to recurring one-off items.
data_conflicts: v4 quant composite (b1_live_scores.csv) ranks DIS poorly (composite 0.167, decile 2, live_rank 414/503) with a negative earnings-momentum/SUE score (0.033) despite management reiterating ~12% FY26 adjusted-EPS growth and raising the buyback target; likely a GAAP-EPS-volatility artefact (impairments, tax items) feeding the SUE calculation rather than genuine deceleration -- flagged, not resolved.
DIS.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the streaming-margin inflection and Parks growth are well evidenced, but this year's FCF decline is real and not yet explained away as pure timing

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for DIS (outside V1's original 69-name universe), so there is nothing to reconcile against; this dossier's own reverse-DCF (implied ~7.5%/yr 10-year FCF growth at a 9% WACC) is judged roughly in line with, arguably marginally below, an evidence-based 7-8%/yr base case.

DLR.thesis_one_line: Largest data-center REIT, riding the AI/hyperscale build with a record leasing backlog, but growth is being funded by heavy equity dilution and rising debt costs.
kill_criteria: Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 5.5x (vs 4.7x now) without a corresponding acceleration in backlog conversion.
FY26 Core FFO/share guidance is cut (vs the current $8.15-$8.20 ex-net-promote range) at the Q3 2026 release (2026-10-22).
Same-capital cash NOI growth falls below 4.0% for two consecutive quarters (vs the 4.25-5.25% FY26 guide).
ATM share issuance for the full year exceeds ~$4bn (vs $2.5bn through Q2) without matching growth in per-share Core FFO -- a sign dilution is outrunning growth.
The SEC cybersecurity-disclosure inquiry results in a material enforcement action or restatement.
key_adverse_facts: Net debt/adjusted EBITDA is 4.7x, elevated for a REIT even though flat-to-improving YoY.
$2.5bn of YTD ATM equity issuance (13.5m shares at avg $184.94) is real, ongoing per-share dilution funding the growth capex.
FY26 development capex guidance raised to $4.25-4.75bn; long-term debt issuance pricing guidance raised to 4.5-5.5% (from 4.0-4.5%), i.e. marginal borrowing costs are rising.
Open, unresolved SEC investigation into the adequacy of DLR's cybersecurity-risk disclosures and disclosure controls; company says immaterial but the matter is not closed.
GAAP diluted EPS is extremely volatile and not meaningful (e.g. $2.94 in Q2 2025 on a one-off gain vs $0.15-$0.46 in adjacent quarters); the triage's raw 62x P/E is a GAAP artefact.
New $3.5bn, 64%-stake joint-venture acquisition of three Northern Virginia hyperscale data centers concentrates counterparty/partner risk.
data_conflicts: Triage flagged net debt/EBITDA of 5.7x as a red flag; the company's own Q2 2026 primary-source disclosure states 4.7x (flat vs Q1 2026, improved from 5.1x a year ago) -- resolved in DLR's favour, but the source of the triage's 5.7x figure was not independently traced this pass.

v4 quant composite ranks DLR poorly (composite 0.161, decile 2, live_rank 417/503) with a very weak Quality-family score (fam_Q 0.035); this is very likely a REIT-accounting artefact (straight-line depreciation, land/building capitalisation distort the generic Quality factor's gross-profit/assets and accruals inputs) rather than a genuine quality problem, per the sector playbook -- flagged, not independently re-derived.
DLR.confidence_in_thesis: medium - leasing/backlog evidence is strong and primary-sourced, but per-share economics depend on continued heavy equity issuance and an unresolved SEC disclosure inquiry

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for DLR (outside V1's original 69-name universe). A generic FCFF reverse-DCF would misvalue this REIT (per the known V1 REIT-FFO flaw already documented in STATE.md); this dossier instead uses P/Core FFO (~21.9x) and a dividend-discount sanity check (implied ~5.3%/yr perpetual distribution growth vs management's guided double-digit near-term Core FFO growth), judged roughly in line with a reasonable base case.

DOV.thesis_one_line: Diversified industrial group riding real AI-data-center cooling demand, low debt, and a share price pricing in far less growth than management is currently delivering.
kill_criteria: Climate & Sustainability Technologies segment organic growth or margin deteriorates for a second consecutive quarter (vs the Q2 2026 refrigeration-driven miss), indicating the production problem is structural, not a one-quarter event.
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance (currently $10.55-$10.75) is cut at the Q3 2026 release (2026-10-22).
Book-to-bill falls below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters (vs 1.06x-1.2x in H1 2026).
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.0x (vs ≈0.8x now) without a value-accretive acquisition justifying it.
The $58.9m ESG jury verdict is upheld on appeal and expands materially beyond the awarded amount, or triggers additional related claims.
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 stock fell 9.7% on a disclosed production-throughput/execution miss in the Climate & Sustainability (refrigeration) segment that cost ~1.0-1.5 points of consolidated organic growth, despite an EPS beat and guidance raise.

A jury returned a ~$58.9m verdict (June 2025) against the Environmental Solutions Group business (sold to Terex in Oct 2024) for breach of contract/inducement of breach of fiduciary duty; post-trial motions filed, appeal to the Seventh Circuit possible.

The October 2024 sale of the Environmental Solutions Group causes a real discontinuity in reported revenue/net income/OCF between FY2024 and FY2025-26 filings; FY2024 GAAP net income ($2,697m) was inflated by the ~$2.0bn divestiture gain.
Polymer Processing (within Pumps & Process Solutions) was flagged as a weak sub-segment despite overall segment margin expansion.
Analysts pressed management on why bookings (+16% YoY) are not translating proportionally into revenue -- a near-term visibility question.
DOV.confidence_in_thesis: high - broad-based order strength (book-to-bill >1.0x across all five segments), low leverage, and a genuine, still-early data-center cooling growth driver are all primary-sourced and mutually consistent; the refrigeration execution miss is a real but contained quality concern

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for DOV (outside V1's original 69-name universe), so there is nothing to reconcile against; this dossier's own reverse-DCF (implied ~4.1%/yr 10-year FCF growth at an 8.5% WACC) is well below an evidence-based 8-9%/yr base case built from FY26 guided adjusted-EPS growth (~13-15% at the midpoint) and book-to-bill above 1.0x across all five segments.
